newsitem.title: TURKEY: U.S. official to meet Iraq Kurd chief - group.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official to meet Iraq Kurd chief - group.

text.p: A senior U.S. State Department official is to meet Iraq's Baghdad-backed Kurdish strongman in Turkey for talks on the search for peace between the feuding Kurds, an Iraqi opposition group said on Tuesday.

The opposition Iraqi Broadcasting Corporation (IBC) said Massoud Barzani, head of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), would travel to Turkey on Thursday to meet Robert Pelletreau, the U.S. assistant secretary of state for near eastern affairs.
The IBC is a wing of the Iraqi National Congress opposition group.

A U.S. official said Pelletreau was in Ankara on Tuesday but could not confirm plans for a meeting with Barzani, whose forces took control of most of northern Iraq last week after defeating the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) of rival warlord Jalal Talabani.
Iraqi troops aided Barzani in earlier stages of the fighting late last month, prompting U.S. missile strikes against targets in southern Iraq.
"The meeting will be to continue U.S. mediation efforts between Mr Barzani and Mr Jalal Talabani," the IBC said in a statement.
Fighting between the two Kurdish factions broke out last month, shattering a ceasefire brokered by Washington last year and increasing the influence of President Saddam Hussein in northern Iraq.

It was not clear where in Turkey the meeting was to be held but a Turkish newspaper reported on Tuesday that Barzani would meet Turkish officials in the border town of Silopi on Thursday for talks on tightening security on the border.
